title: Prosecution asks ICC to include prior testimonies of 5 witnesses in Rodrigo Duterte case
summary: The Prosecution in the case of former president Rodrigo Duterte on Friday asked the International Criminal Court Trial Chamber III to allow the prior recorded testimonies of five witnesses as…

blocks.text: The Prosecution in the case of former president Rodrigo Duterte on Friday asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III to allow the prior recorded testimonies of five witnesses as evidence.

In a 12-page document, a redacted version of which was posted on the ICC website, ICC Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang requested that they be allowed to submit the transcripts and associated material of witnesses P-1087, P-1151, P-1158, P-1161, and P-1204 (referred to as Five Witnesses).

"Granting the request will enhance the expeditiousness of the proceedings by reducing the length of the witnesses’ direct examination from [REDACTED] hours to [REDACTED] hours, thus saving at least [REDACTED] hours of court time," Niang said.
The Five Witnesses' prior recorded testimonies are relevant, reliable, and probative, he added.

"As [REDACTED], the Five Witnesses provide evidence on [REDACTED]. As such, their evidence is particularly relevant to the policy to ‘neutralise’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines and to [REDACTED] to implement this policy," Niang said.

"The introduction into evidence of the Prior Recorded Testimonies is not prejudicial to or inconsistent with the rights of the Accused, as the Five Witnesses will be available for cross examination by the Defence and any further questioning by the Chamber, the parties, and the Common Legal Representatives of Victims (the “CLRV”)," he added.

Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with the alleged extrajudicial killings in the war on drugs during his term as president, and during his term as mayor of Davao City.
He was arrested in March 2025 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 and is currently detained at the ICC Detention Centre in Scheveningen in The Hague, The Netherlands.
Duterte's trial will start on Nov. 30.
The ICC Trial Chamber III found fDuterte fit to stand trial, stating that he “is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings.” —KG, GMA News
